body: Every time I drag the window down and back up (so it's maximized), the title bar buttons keep getting bigger: Minimizing the window fixes it, but the height still seems to big with default size:

> Every time I drag the window down and back up (so it's maximized), the title bar buttons keep getting bigger

Without digging into it too much, I believe that the project manager and editor handle the title bar size weirdly, e.g. doing `window_set_window_buttons_offset` every time the title bar changes. Here is my implementation of a title bar, which I first implemented on mac, where `extend_to_title` is already implemented, and then tweaked and tested with as I implemented this for windows:
https://github.com/MattParkerDev/SharpIDE/blob/main/src/SharpIDE.Godot/Features/SlnPicker/SlnPickerTitleBar.cs

I set WindowSetWindowButtonsOffset once, and nothing ever changes that.

If possible, I would like to avoid too much reworking of project_manager and editor_node - I would be content with disabling extend_to_title for them, for it to be tackled in another PR to enable support on windows. However I understand that if they are misbehaving, it potentially means this implementation is flawed.

> Minimizing the window fixes it, but the height still seems to big with default size: 

I currently set the height as `window_set_window_buttons_offset(Vector2i(23, 22)`, which is much closer to a square than the true windows default rectangle. It is the same dimensions as the caption buttons in firefox for example.

`editor_node` sets the window button offsets here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6d6e822c689acb54bf86e19cc2bbbe3fa567b123/editor/editor_node.cpp#L1642

Which sets the button height/width.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118939#issuecomment-4327380705
> Every time I drag the window down and back up (so it's maximized), the title bar buttons keep getting bigger:

Resolved :)

Enabling either of the window stretch modes or setting a window's `content_scale_factor` to a value other than 1.0 causes the title bar buttons to be offset incorrectly, while also being affected by the scaling.

`get_window().position += Vector2i.ZERO` moves the window and increases it's size.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdffac40-6520-4749-94ee-b2eeb329cac1

Sorry if this was already explained elsewhere. This PR seems to draw the window caption buttons on the Godot side. Doesn't Windows already have a way to make a chromeless window [that still displays](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/title-bar#:~:text=The%20caption%20controls%20%28system%20Close%2C%20Minimize%2C%20and%20Maximize%20buttons%29%20are%20still%20available%20and%20handled%20by%20the%20system%2C%20but%20elements%20like%20the%20app%20title%20are%20not%2E) caption buttons, borders, and shadows?

> Doesn't Windows already have a way to make a chromeless window that still displays caption buttons, borders, and shadows?

This is WinUI3, it's an external dependency that is not part of core Windows API.

I see, this indeed doesn't seem possible with Win32 APIs.
BTW, the example video has the splash screen without caption buttons (and without drag area I presume). Is this a peculiarity of that app or a direct result from this PR? If it's the latter, I think the splash screen shouldn't use extend-to-title then.

Thanks for reporting those issues FLix3r, I will investigate and fix.

@neikeq 

> BTW, the example video has the splash screen without caption buttons (and without drag area I presume). Is this a peculiarity of that app or a direct result from this PR? If it's the latter, I think the splash screen shouldn't use extend-to-title then.

Yes, just a peculiarity of that app - I made the default window borderless, for the splashscreen, then change it to windowed once the app starts. E.g. like Rider's splash screen, although less clear, because the splash screen and actual window are the same size in my case.
@Flix3r both issues resolved :)

@MattParkerDev Thanks! The same scaling issue does also apply to `DisplayServer.window_get_safe_title_margins`, so the transform should probably be applied there as well.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56324270-28ee-423a-ad76-d6b5b0632f41

One other thing is that having the built-in title bar buttons always drawn is a bit inconvenient, especially when we have the tools to create our own. I don't know if this needs it's own proposal or PR, but it would be nice to be able to toggle them, maybe through a Window property.
The title bar buttons should also not be drawn if the window is in fullscreen. Currently it makes them squish together.

> One other thing is that having the built-in title bar buttons always drawn is a bit inconvenient, especially when we have the tools to create our own. I don't know if this needs it's own proposal or PR, but it would be nice to be able to toggle them, maybe through a Window property.

This is probably to match how the setting works on macOS. Although it's possible to hide the caption buttons in macOS as well. In any case, this should be a separate proposal where it can be discussed.

Controls being shown in fullscreen is fixed :) Regarding `window_get_safe_title_margins`, this behaviour is the same and prexisting on macos: bruzvg requested `window_get_safe_title_margins` and `window_set_window_buttons_offset` be in the same units (physical pixels), matching macos. I think this makes sense, so I won't apply any transform there :)

I see, using physical pixels does make sense in that case.
Also, the controls are still shown if fullscreen is set after initialization using `DisplayServer.window_set_mode`.
The title bar buttons become greyed out if an embedded window is focused.

> Also, the controls are still shown if fullscreen is set after initialization using DisplayServer.window_set_mode.

Fixed - display_server_windows emits `WINDOW_EVENT_TITLEBAR_CHANGE` when fullscreen changes - same as MacOS.
Was there anything more needed to be done on this PR? :)

> The title bar buttons become greyed out if an embedded window is focused.

I believe this has not been fixed.

I somewhat left that "unfixed" to get consensus on whether it is a bug or not. 

They are greyed for native windows, and embedded windows have a distinct focus style too - should we special case native root windows with embedded sub windows?

> They are greyed for native windows, and embedded windows have a distinct focus style too - should we special case native root windows with embedded sub windows?

As the buttons are an imitation of OS behavior, I think it makes far more sense for them to behave as those do, and reflect the state of the native OS window.
